title: The Secure Bond: The Emotional Foundation for Every Future Learning
summary: Attachment theory (Bowlby/Ainsworth) is established: a child who feels secure with a responsive parent develops a 'secure base' from which to explore the world with confidence. Consistent response to crying, eye contact, mutual smiling, and physical presence—these build an 'internal working model' of self-worth and trust in others. The 'Early Moments Matter' report (UNICEF) states: the first thousand days shape the brain’s structure—compassionate responsiveness = strong neural connections for emotion and learning. Chronic neglect, meaning a long absence of responsive care, can cause 'toxic stress' that harms brain development, learning and health for years, according to Harvard's Center on the Developing Child.
try_this: This week: when your child cries or calls you, respond warmly and as promptly as you can, even with a word: 'I'm coming, my love.' In the first months you cannot spoil a baby with attention. Start with his most pressing need: is he hungry, cold, tired or in pain, or does his nappy need changing? Notice: does he settle when you respond? Does he go back to play with confidence?
reflection_prompts: How did you experience ease or anxiety as a parent? Do you see its impact on how you interact with your child?
What moment did you feel your child 'trusts' you completely?

review_defects.why: The English reassurance adds 'I'm on my way' to «أنا قادم يا حبيبي» — harmless.
